summary.intent: Complete Phase 23 (Rust SDK Extraction) gap closure execution, run a security review, add test coverage for the new Rust crates, and get PR #352 merged through CI.
summary.outcome: All Phase 23 plans executed and verified; 163 new Rust unit tests added; multiple security findings fixed; PR #352 created and iteratively improved through several rounds of code review resolution. Windows CI cargo check remains unresolved — a debug notes file was committed to the branch for continuation on a Windows machine.

repo: The workspace [workspace.dependencies] entry must have `default-features = false` — consumer-side `{ workspace = true, default-features = false }` alone is insufficient; Cargo requires the workspace-level definition to carry that flag.

cipherbox-fuse uses feature flags `fuse` (Unix/FUSE) and `winfsp` (Windows/WinFSP) to gate platform-specific code; these are mutually exclusive and the CI command is `cargo check --workspace --no-default-features --features winfsp`.

The vendored fuser crate (apps/desktop/src-tauri/vendor/fuser) is always resolved by Cargo due to [patch.crates-io], even when no feature activates it — it must be able to compile as a no-op on Windows.
HKDF domain separation is correct across all 5 derivation contexts; all KeyState and CipherBoxFS key fields use Zeroizing<Vec<u8>> with proper zeroization on logout and unmount.
generate_ed25519_keypair callers were wrapping the return value in redundant Zeroizing::new() — the function itself now returns Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>.
IpnsPublishRequest previously derived Debug, leaking encrypted IPNS key material — replaced with a custom Debug impl that redacts sensitive fields.
The cross-language vector parity test imports @cipherbox/core which depends on @cipherbox/crypto — they must be built sequentially (crypto first) not in parallel.

code.finding: generate_ed25519_keypair now returns Zeroizing<Vec<u8>> for the private key; callers in write_ops.rs removed redundant Zeroizing::new() wrappers
Root workspace dep for cipherbox-fuse needed `default-features = false` — without this, the `fuse` feature was being activated on Windows despite --no-default-features
Vendored fuser wrapped in cfg(unix) via include! pattern — lib_impl.rs holds all real code, lib.rs is empty on non-Unix
Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>.try_into() doesn't work directly for [u8;32] — must use Vec::from(key).try_into() to unwrap first
Bug: app_version and device_model fields were set to device_id due to partial move — fixed by capturing values before the struct move
Temp dir cleanup must happen AFTER unmount, not before — fixed for both Linux and macOS
DeserializationFailed variant used for reqwest errors — corrected to RequestFailed which has the #[from] reqwest::Error impl

workflow: When an agent disconnects mid-execution, check git log for commits and verify acceptance criteria before re-running — often only bookkeeping (SUMMARY.md, STATE.md) remains.
cargo tree -e features is the definitive tool for diagnosing unexpected Cargo feature activation; use it before iterating through CI roundtrips.
Workspace [patch.crates-io] entries are always resolved by Cargo regardless of feature activation — patched crates must compile (even as no-ops) on all target platforms.
1Password SSH agent can be flaky for commit signing; retrying 2-3 times usually resolves it.
Running security review, test coverage, and PR review resolution in parallel (separate agents for each crate) is much faster than sequential execution.
When CI is failing on a platform you can't test locally, commit a debug notes file to the branch before switching machines to preserve context.

friction: 1Password SSH signing agent repeatedly failed, requiring multiple commit retries throughout the session.
Windows cargo check required 7+ CI roundtrips to diagnose — root cause was layered (fuser build.rs → fuser lib.rs → workspace default-features → WinFSP module resolution still unresolved).
Cargo workspace feature resolution is non-obvious: consumer-side `default-features = false` is insufficient without matching workspace-level declaration.
[patch.crates-io] forces crate resolution for ALL workspace members regardless of feature activation, making platform-specific vendored crates problematic.
CodeRabbit reopened the same ecies.rs min-size comment 3 separate times across multiple review rounds.
Cross-language vector parity failure had two separate causes (pnpm version missing, then build order wrong) requiring two CI roundtrips.
open_items: Windows cargo check is still failing — the WinFSP platform modules (read_ops.rs:19, write_ops.rs:20, dir_ops.rs:13) can't find `super::operations` despite winfsp feature being active. Needs local Windows debugging (see .planning/phases/23-rust-sdk-extraction/WINDOWS-BUILD-DEBUG.md).
AES-CTR ciphertext lacks client-side CID integrity verification — HIGH finding from security review, deferred (not fixed in this session).
file_ipns_private_key in write_ops.rs uses ed25519_dalek directly (not generate_ed25519_keypair) and doesn't use Zeroizing — noted as secondary concern, not addressed.

The fuse crate's crate-level operations.rs/read_ops.rs/write_ops.rs/dir_ops.rs are currently only gated by `#[cfg(feature = "fuse")]` — if the workspace fix fully resolves the Windows issue, these may still need cfg(unix) guards for robustness.
